sanmarco: Venice's most famous square, with the Basilica of golden mosaics and five domes, the 98-metre Campanile and the Procuratie on either side. Inside the basilica are the gold-ground mosaics, the undulating floor and the Pala d'Oro.
palazzoducale: Doge's Palace and Bridge of Sighs

The palace of the Doges, symbol of the Venetian Republic's power: the courtyard, the Giants' Staircase, the Great Council halls with Tintoretto's "Paradise" and the Bridge of Sighs, which led to the prisons.
rialto: The oldest stone bridge over the Grand Canal, from 1591, lined with shops, and right after it the Rialto market with its fruit, vegetable and fish stalls and the bacari where you taste cicchetti.
accademia: The museum of Venetian painting, in an old scuola, with works by Titian, Tintoretto, Veronese, Giorgione and Canaletto. You can also see Giorgione's "Tempest" and Carpaccio's great cycle of the legend of St Ursula.
salute: Basilica della Salute and Punta della Dogana

The great domed Baroque church built after the plague of 1630, at the entrance to the Grand Canal. Inside are works by Titian and Tintoretto. From the tip of the Dogana, next to it, you see St Mark's across the basin.
peggy: Peggy Guggenheim's modern art collection in the palazzo on the Grand Canal that was her home: Picasso, Pollock, Kandinsky, Magritte and Dalí, and a sculpture garden.
frari: The great brick Gothic church of the Franciscan friars, with Titian's "Assumption" over the high altar, the tombs of Titian and Canova and a Madonna by Giovanni Bellini in the sacristy.
ghetto: The world's first ghetto, established in 1516: the tall houses on Campo del Ghetto Nuovo, the synagogues and the Jewish Museum. From there you walk along the canals of Cannaregio, a district where many Venetians still live.
castello: The walk along St Mark's basin, eastwards, to the Arsenale and the Giardini: the Castello district is quieter than the centre, with its calli, gardens and the old Republic's shipyards.
zattere: Zattere and the San Trovaso boatyard
The long sunny promenade along the edge of Dorsoduro, facing the Giudecca. Nearby is the Squero di San Trovaso, one of the few yards where gondolas are still built and repaired.
isole: Three islands in the northern lagoon: Murano, with its glass furnaces, Burano, with houses painted red, yellow and blue and its lace, and Torcello, with the 7th-century Byzantine cathedral and the oldest mosaics in the lagoon.
